subject: BrightPath inference ops & policy — post-call action items
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@brightpath.ai>, Samira Lopez <samira@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: BrightPath inference ops & policy — post-call action items

Alex / Samira — great call this morning, thanks for walking us through BrightPath's search-and-personalization use case. Short recap and concrete next steps so we have a shared playbook for the technical work that follows.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary flow: user query -> semantic search over vector store -> top-K results -> re-ranker + structured output generation for candidate extraction (dates, prices, product ids) -> UI render.
- Volume profile: ~1.2M queries/month, 95th percentile query length ~80 tokens, median 8 tokens.
- Latency target: interactive UI with 95th <= 350ms for the combined search+re-rank path.
- Data sensitivity: PII in prompts, contract requires EU data residency for EU customers.

Technical ask / priorities (we discussed)
1) SDK setup & auth: you want a quick start for product engineers (Python + Node), plus SSO/OIDC for service-to-service auth.
2) Routing & policy: per-region routing, latency-first fallback chain, cost tiering for batch/low-priority offline work.
3) Structured output / tool calling: deterministic JSON extraction for the UI, and an optional external tool call to your pricing engine.
4) Embeddings + reranker: nightly embeddings refresh vs on-write, and a hybrid reranker approach (approx NN recall + lightweight cross-attention re-ranker).

Attachments: sending a short mutual_action_plan.xlsx and an updated arch diagram (redwood_arch_diagram_v1.png) that maps SDK -> gateway -> routing layer -> serving pools. See attached stubs.

Immediate next steps (mutual action plan)
- Action 1 (BrightPath): Send a 1-page list of the top 3 example queries + sample doc corpus for embedding tests (due: Tue 18 Nov).
- Action 2 (Redwood SEs): Provision a sandbox Dedicated pool for BrightPath with a US-West region config (we'll include an EU region candidate on request). ETA: Tue 18 Nov.
- Action 3 (Joint): Run a bench with 1K simulated queries to validate 95th latency and reranker accuracy. ETA: Fri 21 Nov.

Questions for you (please confirm)
- Do you prefer API key or OIDC S2S for service accounts (we can support both; OIDC is recommended if you want short-lived creds and audit logs linked to your IdP).
- For EU customers, do you require all inference (model execution) to remain in EU, or is metadata-only in EU acceptable?

I'll loop in a short model-routing policy proposal in a follow-up (Rishi / Laura - adding a concrete policy snippet + config defaults).

Thanks again,

--
Priyom Das

Thanks Priyom — very helpful summary. Quick clarifications from our side before we hand over sample data: 

1) Structured output / tool calling
- We need the output to be a strict JSON schema (we'll validate client-side). Can Redwood guarantee schema-constrained generation (e.g., function calling / JSON schema enforcement) to avoid hallucinated fields?
- For the pricing engine call: do you recommend making that an external tool call from the model or doing it in application code after structured extraction?

2) Reranker latency budget
- Our UI requires the top-K re-ranking to add no more than ~120ms on the 95th. Is that realistic if we do a cross-attention reranker on the top 50 candidates?

3) EU data residency
- For customers in EU, BrightPath's legal requires that inference and embeddings for EU user data remain in EU. We want to understand operational complexity and added cost.

Small ask: can Rishi / Laura share a simple example routing policy and an estimated cost-per-1M queries for the config you propose? We'll need these numbers for procurement.

Also — the MAP attachment looks great. We'll send sample queries + a small doc dump by Tuesday.

Alex

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightPath inference ops & policy — post-call action items

Alex — appreciate the specific questions. Below are concrete answers and a suggested model-routing policy you can review. Rishi / Laura please jump in if I get any technical bits wrong.

1) Schema-constrained generation / function calling
- Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured output enforcement. For strict JSON we recommend: 1) use function-calling with an explicit JSON schema for the extractor; 2) run a low-cost validation pass server-side (we can add a short deterministic post-processor to reject malformed outputs). That gives you high confidence without adding model latency to every request.
- For the pricing engine we generally recommend doing the authoritative price calculation in your application after the model returns structured fields. Use a model-driven tool call only for optional enrichment (e.g., predicted discounts) or to pre-fill inputs — keep the authoritative logic in your pricing service.

2) Reranker latency / architecture trade-offs
- Cross-attention on top-50 will likely exceed your 120ms 95th target in many cases unless the reranker is a tiny distilled model and runs on a low-latency pool. Options:
  - Option A (recommended): ANN recall to top-200 -> fast lightweight re-encoder rerank (vector dot) to top-20 -> tiny cross-attn on top-10. This keeps heavy cross-attn calls small and within latency budgets.
  - Option B: Batch reranking for non-interactive sessions (offline refresh) and cache the top results for interactive queries.

3) EU data residency + operational cost
- We can host inference + embedding pipelines in EU regions (Redwood Private/Dedicated in eu-west1). That satisfies the "inference in-region" requirement.
- Cost delta (rough): expected +15–30% for EU-dedicated pools versus US on-demand due to reserved capacity and region pricing. We'll produce a finer estimate once we define instance types and utilization.

Suggested model routing policy (pseudo-config)
- priority_pools:
  - latency_critical_pool: model: redwood-llm-small-quant, hardware: A10G, region: us-west1, capacity: reserved, max_p95_latency_ms: 220
  - balance_cost_pool: model: redwood-llm-base-8bit, hardware: A100-40g, region: us-west1, capacity: burst, target_cost_per_1k_tokens: low
  - fallback_pool: model: redwood-llm-tiny-quant, hardware: T4, region: any, capacity: on-demand, purpose: last-resort

- routing_rules:
  - rule: ui_short_queries
    match: prompt_length <= 32 AND user_tier == premium
    route_to: latency_critical_pool
  - rule: search_full_path
    match: flow == semantic_search
    route_to: balance_cost_pool
    post_process: kv_cache_enabled
  - rule: exception_fallback
    match: latency_slo_violated OR capacity_exhausted
    route_to: fallback_pool

- reranker_policy:
  - stage1: ANN on embeddings (vector DB in eu-west1/us-west1)
  - stage2: re-encoder scoring on top-200 (cheap vector ops)
  - stage3: cross-attention (top-10) with model: reranker-small, p95 target: 80ms

Notes on monitoring and SLOs
- We will provision token-level tracing and a per-route p95 latency alert. If p95 climbs > 20% above target, automatic policy switches to the fallback chain (rule: exception_fallback).
- We'll include cost telemetry in the dashboard so you can see per-route per-token spend and tune batch/windows.

Deliverables we'll produce this week
- Rishi: sample routing policy JSON + estimated cost-per-1M queries for the proposed pool mix (ETA: Mon 16 Nov).
- Laura: quick SDK starters (Python/Node) that show function-calling schema enforcement and an example reranking pipeline (ETA: Tue 18 Nov).

If that looks good, can we lock a 30-min tech sync for Tue 18 Nov (I propose 10am PST)? I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to the sandbox run.

Best,

--
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147
